summary: AI observability has become one of the most consequential infrastructure decisions for LLM teams, with 73% of enterprises now requiring AI agent monitoring. These tools provide tracing, cost tracking, quality metrics, and guardrails that separate production-grade deployments from teams flying blind. Choosing the right platform depends on your workload type—RAG, agents, chatbots, or combined ML/LLM pipelines—and your need for cost control.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end LLM application traces, multi-step agent workflows, prompts, token usage, latency, and unified workflow costs.
features: Deep multi-step agent debugging and diagnostics
Unified workflow cost tracking across chains
tools.pricing: Free Developer tier (5K traces/mo); Plus plan at $39/seat/month; usage-based and enterprise tiers available.
tools.best_for: Teams building complex multi-step agents (especially on LangChain) needing deep diagnostics and evaluation workflows.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests at the proxy/gateway level—costs, latency, token usage, caching, and request logs.
features: Daily regression testing alongside production traffic
tools.pricing: Free tier (10K requests/mo); usage-based paid plans thereafter.
tools.best_for: Chatbots and teams wanting fast setup with a gateway layer focused on cost control and monitoring.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: ML experiments, model training runs, and LLM traces/evaluations via W&B Weave—tracking metrics, artifacts, and token usage.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free tier for personal/academic use; team and enterprise plans are usage/seat-based (custom pricing).
tools.best_for: ML teams running both traditional ML experiments and LLM apps that want a unified experiment-tracking and observability platform.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Production ML and LLM model performance—drift, data quality, embedding/retrieval quality, and evaluations (via Arize Phoenix for LLMs).
features: Production model monitoring and drift detection
Arize Phoenix open-source tracing and eval
tools.pricing: Phoenix is free/open-source; Arize AX offers a free tier with paid Pro and enterprise plans (custom pricing).
tools.best_for: RAG applications and ML teams needing deep retrieval quality metrics and production drift monitoring.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: LLM application traces, per-LLM-call costs, token usage, latency, prompt performance, and evaluation scores.
tools.pricing: Free open-source self-hosted; managed cloud has a free Hobby tier with Core, Pro, and enterprise paid plans.
tools.best_for: Agent and multi-step LLM apps where teams want an open-source, self-hostable observability stack.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM and vector DB calls via OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation—traces, token usage, latency, and costs exportable to any OTel backend.
features: Vendor-neutral—export to Datadog, Grafana, Honeycomb, etc.
Auto-instrumentation for major LLM providers and frameworks
Vector database and embedding call tracing
Minimal lock-in by building on existing OTel stack
tools.pricing: Free and open-source; costs depend on the chosen OTel backend (Traceloop offers a hosted managed option with paid tiers).
tools.best_for: Teams that want vendor-neutral, standards-based instrumentation feeding into their existing observability backend.

cost_tips: Use a gateway/proxy layer (e.g., Helicone or Portkey) with response caching to avoid paying for repeated or identical requests.
Right-size your models—route simple tasks to smaller, cheaper models and reserve frontier models for complex reasoning.
Optimize prompts and context windows by trimming unnecessary tokens, truncating history, and using concise system prompts.
Set budget alerts, rate limits, and per-feature cost tracking so you can catch runaway spend and attribute costs accurately.
